item.title: listItems follows next_cursor
item.brief: Update listItems(transport) in inventory-client so it resolves to every item, in order, by following next_cursor until it is null or absent. The first request sends no cursor; each later request passes the previous next_cursor back unchanged. Keep the existing listItems(transport) signature. Add tests with a fake transport that serves multiple pages, a single page, an empty result, and a response where next_cursor is absent, and assert the exact cursor values sent. Update the README to describe the paging behaviour. Run `npm test` and make it pass. Commit in this repository only; do not push.

item.title: Cursor pagination in GET /items
item.brief: Add cursor pagination to GET /items in inventory-api, following the shared contract exactly. Accept optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous next_cursor); return {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>} with items ordered by id and next_cursor null on the last page. Return HTTP 400 with {"error": "..."} for an invalid limit or cursor. Add unit tests covering: default page size, limit bounds (0, 1, 100, 101, non-integer), cursor round-trip across all pages with no gaps or duplicates, next_cursor null on last page, and invalid cursor -> 400. Update the README to document the query parameters, response shape and 400 errors. Keep functions short and validate inputs at the boundary. Run `python3 -m unittest` and make it pass. Commit in this repository only; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: cursor is base64url of the last returned item id; next page is items with id greater than cursor id. Key files: api.py (list_items, parse_limit, parse_cursor, encode_cursor), test_api.py (5 new paging tests), README.md (query params, response shape, 400 errors). Checks: python3 -m unittest, 9 tests OK. Assumptions: item ids are unique positive ints. inventory-client listItems is out of scope for this item. Follow-ups from review (non-blocking): cursor decoding is non-validating base64; cursor decoding to 0 is accepted; add tests for cursor with non-default limit on final page and cursor past last id.
pr.summary: Made GET /items paginate. Now can page with limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor. Before: all 57 items, no next_cursor; now: one page plus next_cursor, null on last page; invalid limit or cursor returns 400.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

agt_01M8GR081WTWV56DEAXNXDF0BG:1.description: parse_cursor uses non-validating base64 (validate=False), so junk characters are discarded and non-canonical encodings such as 'MQ==xyz' are accepted as id 1. Opacity is loose; consider validate=True or a re-encode comparison.

agt_01M8GR081WTWV56DEAXNXDF0BG:2.description: A cursor that decodes to 0 (e.g. 'MA==') is accepted even though the API never issues it. Consider rejecting ids below 1 with 400.

agt_01M8GR081WTWV56DEAXNXDF0BG:3.description: Untested: a cursor combined with a non-default limit on the final partial page, and a cursor past the last id (returns an empty page with null next_cursor, which is correct).

risk.why: Contained additive feature behind the existing handle() interface: optional limit and cursor params, no change to existing GET /items callers, no security, persistence, concurrency or breaking API change. Reviewer agt_01M8GR081WTWV56DEAXNXDF0BG confirmed medium.
